newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - April 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - April 2.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY
- President Jiang Zemin issues directive to award group of People's Liberation Army units and individuals citations for merit.
- Chinese President Jiang Zemin tells visiting Australian Prime Minister John Howard that China and Australia should further cooperation.
XINHUA DAILY TELEGRAPH
- President Jiang Zemin hails signing of memorandum of understanding on submarine optical cable project between AT&T and China.
- Average speed of China's trains upgraded while price of tickets remains unchanged.
CHINA SECURITIES
- China to regulate domestic insurance market, including shutting unauthorised branches
FINANCIAL NEWS
- Central bank wants faster withdrawal of cash from circulation
- State Planning Commission issue circular to check prices of farm materials during spring sowing season
- China Merchant Bank makes 2.423 billion yuan in profits in 1996
ECONOMIC DAILY
- China treasury bond underwriters urged to sell state debt to farmers
ECONOMIC INFORMATION DAILY
- Zhejiang province to cut number of silk reeling machines to 35,000 from current 61,000
- Harbin Railway Bureau to shed 30,000 workers in next four years
CHINA BUSINESS TIMES
- Editorial sees China unlikely to cut interest rates in 1997
- More than 240,00 people killed or injured in traffic accidents in 1996
- China's first joint venture railway between Jinhua and Wenzhou expected to open in 1997
MARKET DAILY
- China exports first batch of 21 ostriches to North Korea
CHINA DAILY
- Government launches plan to virtually eliminate poverty in China by year 2000, and 17 million people are expected to be lifted out of poverty each year.
- China issues order to ban imports of hogs, oxen, sheep and other two-toed ruminants and by-products from Taiwan following outbreak of foot and mouth disease on island.
- China to host world's third largest show featuring latest advances in metals industry.
